stages.common_vs_different: IDENTICAL failure signature across all three repos: every 'retained unit without candidate destination' error is a heading whose ledger-side heading_text never resolves via compiled_blocks.get(heading) at commands_poc.py L191. Two independent, stacking causes: (a) GRANULARITY -- H3+ sub-headings (e.g. '### Native and System Requirements', '### Scene graph') are never keys in compiled_slot_blocks at all, because that dict is keyed only at top-level contract-slot granularity, not per nested sub-heading; (b) CASE/WORDING -- top-level H2 slot headings DO have a compiled_slot_blocks entry, but the lookup key is the SOURCE README's own spelling ('## Key capabilities', sentence case) while compiled_slot_blocks is keyed by the CONTRACT's canonical Title-Case name ('Key Capabilities'), so even a genuinely-retained top-level slot fails the exact-string lookup. 3D shows both failure modes purely (H1 and 'Navigation' are non-slot headings; H2 slot headings fail on case; H3 sub-headings fail on granularity) despite freshness: current, ruling out import staleness as a contributing factor.

stages.common_vs_different: THIS is where Note diverges from Barcode/3D, and it is a SEPARATE mechanism from stage 7. Note's deterministic_verdict is 'reject' solely because 2 claim-accountability records remain unresolved (blocking_claim_ids); Barcode and 3D have claim_accountability_complete: true and deterministic_verdict: accept. All three independently share the SAME stage-7 ledger failure regardless of stage-8 outcome -- fixing stage 7 would not change Note's stage-8 rejection, and fixing stage 8 would not change any repo's stage-7 ledger validity. aspose_checks: false is common to all three and not investigated further within the time-box (see REPORT.md).

diagnostic_only_locations.detail: validation.json itself carries acceptance_authority: false and an explicit acceptance_exclusion string stating the poc runner bypasses the mission graph, durable lifecycle, recovery, and the supervisor transaction.

blocking_locations.detail: _validate_bundle raises ExceptionAcceptanceError when validation.get('disposition_ledger_valid') is not True or disposition_ledger_errors is non-empty. This is the ONLY other reader of disposition_ledger_valid in the repository (confirmed via grep across src/, scripts/, tests/). As of this run, it would refuse to promote ALL THREE calibration repos, including Barcode and 3D whose deterministic_verdict is otherwise a clean accept.

freshness_service_lane_overlap.finding: YES, overlapping. plans/investigations/evidence/freshness-service-t5/closeout.md (2026-08-15) and its duplicate under freshness-service-final-2026-08-15/t5-closeout.md document a prior fix ('T5') to this exact defect class: compiled_slot_blocks() was added, threaded through ReadmeDocumentPlanV1, and build_source_disposition_ledger's target lookup was wired to it, specifically to fix a 'plain string mismatch' between the source heading's literal '##' prefix and the bare contract heading key, resolved with heading.lstrip('#').strip() (still present today at commands_poc.py L190).
freshness_service_lane_overlap.gap: The T5 fix's own regression tests (tests/unit/test_template_compiler_slot_blocks.py) use a synthetic fixture whose section dict keys ('installation', 'key_capabilities', ...) already produce contract titles textually identical in wording to what a real repository would need ('Installation', 'Key Capabilities'), and the fixture has no nested H3 sub-headings. Neither the case/wording-drift failure mode nor the sub-heading-granularity failure mode this calibration run exposes is exercised by T5's own tests or (per its closeout doc) its single live-pilot re-run. The freshness-service lane is therefore already the owning lane for this code and left it in a partially-fixed state, not a lane that is currently free to hand this off to.

root_cause_summary.note_rejects_because: Stage 8 (deterministic acceptance) finds 2 unresolved claim-accountability records (blocking_claim_ids: candidate:claim:4579:7ff54c1da64deecb, source:claim:4064:7ff54c1da64deecb) via claim_accountability_validation.py::validate_claim_accountability_map, which document_validation.py folds into claim_accountability_complete: false and deterministic_verdict: reject. This is unrelated to the disposition ledger and unique to Note among the three calibration repos.
root_cause_summary.all_three_report_disposition_ledger_vali: Stage 7's build_source_disposition_ledger performs an exact-string lookup of each ledger unit's raw source heading text against compiled_slot_blocks -- a dict keyed only at top-level contract-slot granularity using contract-normalized (Title-Case, canonical-wording) keys. Source headings at any deeper level (H3+) can never be keys in that dict (granularity mismatch), and even top-level H2 slot headings fail whenever the source repository's own heading spelling/case differs from the contract's canonical title (case/wording mismatch). Both failure modes are systemic to any real repository README and independent of imported-knowledge freshness (proven by 3D's freshness: current control case still failing identically).
root_cause_summary.is_it_stale_evidence: No -- ruled out by 3D's freshness: current case failing identically to Note/Barcode's freshness: stale_revision cases.
root_cause_summary.is_it_missing_equivalence_linkage: No -- compiled_slot_blocks is present, correctly populated, and correctly keyed by contract slot name (stage 5 confirmed intact for all three repos).
root_cause_summary.is_it_bad_identity_normalization: Yes -- this is the closest fit. The ledger's target lookup treats the source heading string as if it were already contract-normalized (only '#'-stripped), never applying the same case/wording canonicalization the template compiler itself uses to derive compiled_slot_blocks' keys, and never resolving a sub-heading to its enclosing top-level slot.
root_cause_summary.is_it_source_placement_loss: No -- stage 4/5 evidence shows every relevant section's content genuinely present in the compiled candidate; only the ledger's own bookkeeping fails to record where it landed.
root_cause_summary.is_it_acceptance_fail_open_behavior: No -- the opposite: the diagnostic runner correctly fails CLOSED (disposition_ledger_valid: false, acceptance_authority: false) and the one real acceptance gate that reads this field (promote_working_condition_exceptions.py) also fails closed, correctly refusing promotion. The defect is a false-negative in a fail-closed check, not a fail-open gap.

first_incorrect_transition.detail: target = compiled_blocks.get(heading) where heading = unit.get('heading_text','').lstrip('#').strip() -- an exact-string, single-level dict lookup with no case/wording canonicalization and no ancestor-slot resolution for nested headings. When this lookup misses, target stays '' , which _disposition_acceptance (L292-296) then reports as 'retained unit without candidate destination'.
